text:
maria: Quick share — ran a seqlen-aware kernel sweep for GQA/MQA with paged-kv. Results look noisy: at seqlen ~384 we see a p99 uplift when autotune picks block_size=64 (hotcache hit ~0.62). Baseline (block=128) was cleaner.
kevin: Can you paste the raw numbers? p95/p99 and throughput delta?
sam: curious if this is MQA-only or both GQA/MQA.
maria: Baseline (block=128): p95=23ms p99=42ms throughput=900 tok/s. Autotuned (block=64): p95=24ms p99=45ms throughput=920 tok/s. So throughput +2% but tail +7%. More pronounced on MQA.
kevin: OK that's a meaningful tail shift. Any correlation with hotcache evictions or prefetch spikes?
maria: I profiled the kvcache events. When block=64 we trigger ~1.6x more prefetch ops per request and the kvstripe scatter increases. Quick log snippet: 
```
[perf] seqlen=384 requests=12000 hotcache_hit=0.62 prefetch_ops=18500 kernel_switches=87 p99=45.2ms
[baseline] seqlen=384 requests=12000 hotcache_hit=0.74 prefetch_ops=11200 kernel_switches=12 p99=42.1ms
```
sam: That smells like fragmentation + prefetch churn. MQA has extra queueing and multiq mapping so the smaller block makes more short-lived fragments.
aaron: Hypothesis: smaller blocks reduce wasted kv storage but raise metadata ops and prefetch frequency; combined with MQA's parallel streams increases contention. We should add hysteresis to the autotuner so it doesn't flip for mid-range seqlens.
maria: I implemented a simple hysteresis: require 5k sustained requests with hotcache >= 0.7 before committing block=64, and a conservative fallback to block=128 if p99 exceeds baseline+2ms over a 1-minute window. Early lab runs show p99 back to ~42.5ms while keeping throughput +1.5%.
ci-bot: CI: nightly-profiles/job/987 finished — regression check: p99 +0.8% vs baseline (within tolerance).
kevin: Nice. Can you add telemetry for kvcache_prefetch_count and kernel_switch_count (per minute) so we have direct observability? Also tag the canary with experiment id. :eyes:
sam: And run an A/B canary on a small dedicated pool with MQA-heavy traces. Fallthrough to block=128 if p99 > 44ms for more than 30s.
maria: Will do. Experiment id: 2026-03-kernel-sweep-05. I'll open a tiny PR with the autotune hysteresis config + metrics + canary rollout plan and assign @kevin for review. Expect PR in ~3h. :thumbsup:
kevin: ack, will review. If canary looks good we can flip the default for autoscaler in the next minor.
maria: Summary: keep seqlen-aware kernel selection and smaller blocks for high-hotcache steady workloads, but add hysteresis + p99 fallback to avoid mid-range seqlen regressions. Next steps: PR + canary + dashboard widgets for kvcache_prefetch_count and kernel_switch_count.
kevin: Sounds good. Thanks for the dig.
